title: UConn's 12-0 Finish Stuns Duke
dek: Down 75-67 with 3:28 left, UConn rallied with a 12-0 run behind Emeka Okafor, who sat most of the first half with two fouls, then scored 18.

facts.tip: 8:47 p.m. ET (scheduled; second national semifinal, after Georgia Tech-Oklahoma State)

setup.text: UConn, the preseason No. 1, had lived up to the billing in March, winning four NCAA tournament games by an average of about 17 points. Ben Gordon had scored a Big East tournament-record 81 points and was named the Phoenix Regional's most outstanding performer.

Duke, 31-5 and the top seed out of the Atlanta Regional, had won its four tournament games by an average of 19 points, and Mike Krzyzewski needed one more NCAA tournament win to tie Dean Smith's record of 65. For once, the Blue Devils were cast as the underdog.

It was the programs' first NCAA tournament meeting since UConn's upset in the 1999 title game. UConn's All-American center, Emeka Okafor, had been limited by back spasms and a pinched nerve, and had also dealt with shoulder trouble in the postseason.

story.text: UConn jumped out 15-4, the last five points on a Charlie Villanueva 3-pointer and layup. But Okafor was called for two fouls in the first 3 minutes 55 seconds, and under Jim Calhoun's decades-old two-foul rule he sat the rest of the half, 16:05 on the bench.

Duke answered with a 15-1 run, scoring inside again and again; Shavlik Randolph made all four of his first-half shots. The Blue Devils led by 10 late in the half and 41-34 at the break, then pushed it to 45-34 early in the second half.

Okafor picked up a third foul early in the second half and sat again, then returned with 14:23 left. With about nine minutes to go he soared to block a Luol Deng drive and hit a short jumper at the other end to make it 59-58.

Fouls piled up, 44 in all, and Duke's big men paid: Shelden Williams fouled out with 5:04 left. Daniel Ewing's 3-pointer still pushed Duke ahead 73-64, and Rashad Anderson answered with a 3 of his own.

sequence.text: Ben Gordon is called for his fourth foul, and Chris Duhon makes both free throws. Duke leads by eight and will not score again until the final second.
Shavlik Randolph fouls out, the second Duke big man gone. Okafor misses the free throw.
Luol Deng misses a 3, Taliek Brown boxes out for the rebound, and Rashad Anderson hits a 3 from the corner. The 12-0 run has begun.
Daniel Ewing misses a jumper, Gordon rebounds and is fouled by Duhon, and Gordon makes both free throws.
Okafor forces Duhon to alter a drive and Josh Boone comes up with the loose ball. UConn calls its last timeout.
Gordon dumps the ball inside to Okafor, whose turnaround jumper over Nick Horvath makes it a one-point game.
Deng misses a 3-pointer and UConn gets the ball back.
Okafor's shot rattles out; the rebound is tipped around, and Okafor wrests it away and puts it back in. UConn leads for the first time since midway through the first half.
Out of Krzyzewski's last timeout, J.J. Redick drives and is stripped by Okafor and Anderson. Anderson is fouled by Horvath as he comes up with the loose ball, and makes both free throws.
Needing a 3, Duke goes back to Redick. His tying try falls short, and Okafor rebounds.
Horvath fouls out, Duke's third big man to go, and Okafor makes one of two free throws.
Duhon banks in a long 3 at the buzzer. It only trims the final margin to one.

quotes.text: I grabbed it, spun, saw the rim, thought it would be a good idea to put it in, and that's what I did.
I told him, 'I might put you back in.' Blatant lie.
quotes.when: postgame, on keeping Okafor benched in the first half

quotes.text: I love my team and I'm sorry it was such a crushing defeat.
I would be lying if I said I didn't think about losing the game.

aftermath.text: UConn advanced to Monday's final against Georgia Tech, a 67-65 winner over Oklahoma State on Will Bynum's driving layup with 1.5 seconds left, and the team that had beaten the Huskies 77-61 in November.
Krzyzewski's wait for the NCAA tournament win that would tie Dean Smith's record carried into the next season.
Two nights later UConn beat Georgia Tech 82-73 for its second national championship.

legacy.text: UConn had now won both of the programs' Final Four meetings, the 1999 final and this semifinal, after Duke won their first three NCAA tournament matchups, including the 1990 East Regional final, 79-78 in overtime.
In a WTIC radio countdown of its top 10 UConn games, this one ranked No. 10.
